Priya — quick summary and recommended plan (details + diagrams in attached apac_node_tiling_v3.pdf):

TL;DR recommendation
- Initial active capacity: 24 H100-equivalent GPUs (6 nodes x 4x H100-sim), plated as three AZs: 2 nodes Singapore, 2 nodes Sydney, 2 nodes standby in Singapore for failover.
- Pre-warm buffer: +20% (keep 5 GPUs warm per region) to absorb the 10-minute 12k concurrent bursts without cold starts.
- Autoscale policy: fast-scale for short bursts (scale-out aggressive, scale-in conservative with 10–15min cooldown) and be prepared to route to a lower-cost eu/us fallback region if sustained beyond 20 mins.
- KV/prefix caching: We suggest persistent KV cache replication to both SG and SYD zones; priming job included in our ops checklist.

Sizing rationale (short):
- Orchids’ profile shows 12k concurrent chat sessions in bursts. Assuming a ~120 token avg request and our optimized H100 per-token throughput, 24 GPUs with continuous batching and prefix cache will meet 99p latency target 250ms for chat in most simulated traces (see attached heatmap).
- If Orchid insists on 99.9p SLAs, we should step to 36 GPUs to provide headroom for noisy neighbors and network variability.

Lead times and procurement:
- If we allocate from spare Dedicated inventory in APAC, activation lead: 2–3 business days for config + pre-warm. If new hardware provisioning required, estimate 6–8 weeks.

Risk notes and mitigations:
- Network egress/regional routing — ensure Orchid’s traffic is pinned to regional endpoints; otherwise cross-region egress will add tail latency.
- Model quantization tradeoffs — propose int8-quantized variant for burst windows if Orchid accepts small quality delta, reduces GPU need by ~30%.

Attachments: apac_node_tiling_v3.pdf (tiling diagrams, heatmaps, attempt-level latency sims).

If this looks good I can turn this into a one-page commitment note + pricing sketch for Priya to share.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Hi Evan — thanks for the profile. We ran an ops + capacity pass and propose the following to support your Q4 pilot:

What we propose (summary)
- Initial commitment: a 3-month reserved pool sized at 24 H100-equivalent GPUs (deployed as 6 nodes across SG/SYD).
- Pre-warm: we’ll maintain a 20% warm buffer in-region to hit sub-250ms 99p for chat bursts.
- Burst & scale: aggressive short-burst autoscaling and optional cross-region fallbacks if you want an added reliability layer.
- Lead time: 2–3 business days if we pull from existing APAC reserved inventory and accept an ops handover; 6–8 weeks if this requires new hardware.

Next actions
1) If you want the faster activation (2–3 day), sign the attached commitment sketch and we’ll schedule the pre-warm runbook.
2) If you prefer smaller GPU count during bursts, we can test int8-quantized runtime for a 30% resource reduction — requires a short model-quality smoke test.
3) Ops kick-off: Karthik will own technical onboarding and Ben will coordinate SOW/pricing with your procurement team.

I’ve attached the node-tiling diagram and latency simulations for your review. If this aligns we can do a 30-min technical sync tomorrow to walk through pre-warm and routing (Karthik to lead).
